data.title: Meta built humanoid prototype in robotics push: The Information
data.description:
• Meta Platforms (META) has developed a ‌prototype humanoid robot ​in collaboration with the Chinese ​startup Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the initiative.
  • The roughly 106-pound humanoid identified internally as Max was built in just three months, according to the report. The initiative comes as the Facebook owner doubles down on its efforts to develop robots that people can use in their homes.
  • The goal is to unveil a more polished future product at its robotics division that the social media firm could eventually launch commercially, one of the people said. However, no launch target has been set yet, they added. Meta (META) didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

data.title: Binance restores 90% of stolen crypto assets
data.description:
Binance said on Saturday that it has covered 90% of cryptocurrency assets affected by a massive cyberattack this week, and the company remains on track to resume withdrawals by Sunday within its previously stated timeline.

In a statement on X, the world’s largest crypto exchange said that the remaining 10% of the stolen assets consist of less liquid tokens, which means that the time it takes to replenish them will be longer.

Binance initiated the recoveries after disclosing on Friday that a security incident impacted about $6.3B of client assets, which it said will be fully covered using its own funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users established in 2018.

Shares of crypto exchange Coinbase Global (COIN) and Bitcoin buyer Strategy (MSTR) fell after the announcement, and several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group (CRCL), froze funds linked to the hack.

“We will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and OTC channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens," Binance said. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.”

Fully recovered assets include Bitcoin USD (BTC-USD), Ethereum USD (ETH-USD), Tether USD (USDT-USD), Binance Coin USD (BNB-USD), Solana USD (SOL-USD), USDC (USDC-USD), Ripple USD (XRP-USD), and ZCash USD (ZEC-USD).

data.title: Real estate stocks shine in October amid broader tech rout, lower long-term borrowing costs
data.description:
Real estate stocks outperformed the broader markets in October as rotation out of technology stocks benefited the sector, while the Federal Reserve held its rates steady.

The broader AI sector faced a reality check after OpenAI revised its annualized revenue expectations downward, triggering heavy investor scrutiny over the sustainability of massive infrastructure capital expenditures.

The Cboe Volatility Index surged to a four-month high during the month amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed, reflecting fresh tech struggles.

Persistent technology trade selloff led to major market averages declining in October ahead of the midterm elections.

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump signed an executive order this month that aims to reduce the cost of owning a home. The order directs Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to create a pilot program to cancel borrowers' mortgage insurance premiums proactively once the borrowers have satisfied their equity requirements based on current market value.

Furthermore, long-term borrowing costs decreased during the month. The United States 10-Year Bond Yield (US10Y) fell by 35 basis points to 4.93%. The United States 30-Year Bond Yield (US30Y) reduced by 32 basis points to 5.31%.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 4.98% during the month to 275.07 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was up 5.52% to $43.17.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index rose 4.68%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 4.58% during the course of the week.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) led the gainers, advancing 19.81% to $359.79. The real estate services provider reported a third-quarter earnings beat.

Data center REITs Equinix (EQIX) (+6.14% W/W to $1,013.70) and Iron Mountain (IRM) (+5.99% W/W to $116.55) were gaining ahead of the U.S. midterm elections despite a technology rout this week.

On the election day, voters in 10 U.S. states are set to decide whether to curb data center development in their communities.

Extra Space Storage (EXR) followed with a 5.52% addition to $151.32, benefitting from financial results that exceeded analyst expectations, while the full-year core FFO guidance was raised.

CoStar Group (CSGP) led the losers in the category. The stock fell 11.06% week-over-week to $30.17 after releasing its Q3 financial results and disclosing a deal to acquire Vexcel for $730M.

Sun Communities (SUI) lost 5.81% to close the week at $113.26 as Q3 revenue missed analyst estimates.

For the midcap decliners, Compass (COMP) (-7.69% W/W to $9.00) led the pack.

The stock's price target was lowered at JPMorgan and UBS. Higher mortgage rates and slowing luxury activity reduce near-term earnings visibility for the company, according to UBS.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities (ARE) followed with a 6.56% pull back to $40.20 despite the company turning in stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings and revenue even as its occupancy rate dipped and same-store net operating income slipped from a year ago.

The life sciences campus landlord refined its guidance for the full-year 2026 adjusted FFO per share to $6.38-$6.42, vs. its previous outlook of $6.35-$6.45.

Cushman & Wakefield (CWK) led the midcap gainers, adding 12.43% week-over-week to $13.30 ahead of its Q3 earnings release. The company is expected to post an EPS of $0.36 (+22.95% Y/Y) and revenue of $2.79B (+7.11% Y/Y).

For the smallcap stocks, PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust (PMT) (+6.11% W/W to $7.47), Chatham Lodging Trust (CLDT) (+5.13% W/W to $14.75), Arbor Realty Trust (ABR) (-26.71% W/W to $2.14), Farmland Partners (FPI) (-17.76% W/W to $8.43), and Medical Properties Trust (MPT) (-16.67% W/W to $2.25) were the notable movers.

data.title: Nike has a new plan for retro Michael Jordan shoes
data.description:
Nike's (NKE) Jordan Brand has been one of the growth drivers for the company since it was created in 1997, following 13 years of spectacular sales for Michael Jordan's basketball shoes. Until the last three years, the Jordan brand was still posting positive sales growth even as the rest of the athletic apparel company struggled, and the brand reached a peak of $8.7B in revenue in fiscal year 2024. However, by the end of fiscal 2026, it was down about 20% from that level, and in the first quarter of FY27, Jordan brand revenue fell by a mid-teens percentage.

One of the causes of the downturn may be overexposure. On Nike's (NKE) last earnings conference call, CEO Elliott Hill noted that the company may have been oversupplying its iconic retro product. "And as we've done with the Air Jordan 1, we will deliberately reduce the volume and frequency of specific Jordan Retro launches. We've discussed it with our wholesale partners. Together, we will restore balance to the marketplace to create a foundation for more profitable and sustainable growth," he highlighted. Looking ahead, BNP Paribas sees upside for Nike (NKE) if the Jordan brand can benefit from getting away from frequent discounts, social media trends, and a recovery in resale prices. The success of Nike (NKE) in reinvigorating the Jordan brands has major implications for Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS), especially for the Foot Locker business. 

Nike (NKE) scored one of the biggest coups in retail history when it signed Michael Jordan to a $2.5M endorsement deal in 1984 that was revolutionary at the time in creating an entire product marketing strategy around a single athlete. The continued global sensation of the Air Jordan basketball shoe line eventually led to the creation of the Jordan brand in 1997 as a major subsidiary of the company and dominant force in the footwear industry.

Shares of Nike (NKE) have perked up since the company issued its fiscal first-quarter earnings report, with a 9% swing higher.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 83% of reporting firms beat EPS estimates, 79% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Earnings season reaches peak intensity this week, with 177 companies reporting quarterly results across mega-cap technology, pharmaceuticals, energy, aerospace, and consumer goods.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 177 companies reporting, 147 exceeded EPS expectations, while 26 fell short and 4 matched estimates. Notably, 140 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.

Top Line: Out of the 177 companies reporting, 129 exceeded revenue expectations, while 48 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 157 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) shares were down 0.16% after the Windows maker reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $92.3B (up 19% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of $4.89 (beating expectations). Driven by surging cloud and AI demand, Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9B (up 30% Y/Y), with Azure growing 48% YoY to $33.17B. For Q2 FY27, the company projects revenue between $96.0B and $97.1B, with Azure growth expected at 49%–50% in constant currency.

Amazon.com (AMZN) shares fell 1.4% as capital expenditure and sales guidance overshadowed results. Q3 net sales rose 12% Y/Y to $201.9B, while AWS revenue accelerated to $46.0B (up 39% Y/Y) with an operating backlog reaching $578B. Amazon guided Q4 net sales to $240B–$247B and expects full-year cash CapEx of approximately $220B.

Alphabet (GOOG) shares fell 12.3% following Q3 results, as investors focused on increased capital expenditure despite double-digit top-line expansion. Consolidated revenue rose 25% Y/Y to $127.6B, with Google Cloud jumping 103% to $30.7B. EPS stood at $2.12 ($2.87 on a comparable GAAP basis).

Intel Corporation (INTC) shares fell 28.6% post-earnings after posting Q3 revenue of $16.5B (up 21% Y/Y) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52, topping estimates. Growth was anchored by the Data Center and AI group, which surged 78% Y/Y to $7.3B. For Q4, Intel guides revenue of $15.0B–$16.0B with non-GAAP EPS of $0.25.

The Boeing Company (BA) stock fell 10.7% post-earnings as Q3 revenue of $24.19B (+4% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of -$0.34 missed estimates of $24.37B and -$0.20. Net loss narrowed sharply to $116M (from $5.34B a year ago), with free cash flow rising to $464M despite a ~$700M DOJ settlement payment. Growth in Defense (+15% Y/Y to $7.94B) helped cushion Commercial Airplanes losses (-3% Y/Y to $10.72B), while total backlog hit a record $745B.

AbbVie (ABBV) rose 1.4% after posting a Q3 double beat with revenue of $17.40B (+10% Y/Y) and adjusted EPS of $3.82 (vs. $3.77 consensus). Skyrizi ($5.8B, +23% Y/Y) and Rinvoq ($2.7B, +24% Y/Y) offset Humira's decline ($683M, -31% Y/Y), prompting AbbVie to raise its FY26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint to $13.97.

Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM) rose 2.2% after reporting a Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $4.23 on revenue of $113.16B, topping consensus estimates. Operating cash flow hit $25.7B, supported by 4.5M koebd in oil-equivalent production. The company extended its dividend increase streak to 44 consecutive years with a $1.07 Q4 payout and targeted $20B in share buybacks for 2027.

Altria Group (MO) rose 1.7% after delivered a Q3 double beat with revenue rising 3.4% Y/Y to $5.44B (beating estimates by $130M) and adjusted EPS reaching $1.52 (vs. $1.51 consensus). Backed by steady top-line growth, Altria set its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.66–$5.74 (vs. $5.68 consensus), representing 4.5% to 6.0% Y/Y growth.

PayPal Holdings  (PYPL) shares rose 2% post-earnings after delivering a Q3 double beat driven by expanding total payment volume and branded checkout growth. Supported by disciplined margin execution, PayPal raised its full-year 2026 profitability guidance.

Ford Motor Company (F) shares rose 3.4% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $46.08B and adjusted EPS of $0.49, beating market forecasts. Solid execution in Ford Pro and commercial lineups prompted Ford to narrow and raise its full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5B–$11.0B (up from $10.0B–$11.0B), while reaffirming adjusted free cash flow guidance of $6.0B–$7.0B.

Earnings next week:

The earnings season accelerates next week with key reports across tech, healthcare, consumer, and real estate sectors. Apple (AAPL) leads the tech lineup alongside AI and semiconductor favorites AMD (AMD), Qualcomm (QCOM), Palantir (PLTR), Super Micro Computer (SMCI), and LITE (LITE). Consumer and mobility highlights include McDonald's (MCD), Uber (UBER), and Block (XYZ), while healthcare leaders Pfizer (PFE), CVS Health (CVS), and Viatris (VTRS) also report alongside real estate heavyweights Realty Income (O), Iron Mountain (IRM), and Volaris Group (VMRK).

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: Energy stocks wrap up strong week with near-clean sweep on results
data.description:
Energy stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested a wave of third-quarter earnings, led by major reports from oil giants Exxon Mobil (XOM), Chevron (CVX), and refiner Phillips 66 (PSX).

While uncertainty around energy prices can influence earnings expectations across the sector, companies trading at discounts to their fundamentals may offer opportunities for investors looking for growth at a reasonable price.

In this week's earnings recap, seven tickers reported results, out of which six companies exceeded EPS expectations, while one missed expectations. Except for EQT Corp (EQT), all companies topped revenue expectations.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some of the key players who reported results this week:

  • ExxonMobil (XOM) rose Friday after posting Q3 adjusted earnings that beat Wall Street expectations, capitalizing on the strength of surging gasoline and diesel prices that lifted its refining results to an all-time high. ExxonMobil (XOM) plans to spend more than $100B through 2030 to boost global energy supplies, including ~10% focused on its refining business, particularly at its existing facilities, including the Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Beaumont, Texas, refineries, to improve production yields and raise refined product margins.
  • Shares in Chevron (CVX) also advanced after reporting Q3 adjusted earnings and revenues that topped Wall Street expectations, boosted by higher margins on refined product sales and higher crude oil realizations.
  • Phillips 66 (PSX) closed up 1.9% in Wednesday's trading after reporting its highest-ever quarterly profit that also beat Wall Street estimates, powered by strength in its refining business as the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have disrupted global supplies of diesel and other fuels, pushing prices higher.
  • Baker Hughes (BKR) fell 5.4% in Wednesday's trading despite reporting better than expected Q3 adjusted earnings and revenues, as the Middle East conflict dented demand for oilfield services and equipment in the region.

data.title: S&P 500 materials sector: Four companies miss EPS estimates, six fall short on revenue
data.description:
Twelve of the 24 S&P 500 Materials-sector companies have reported third-quarter 2026 results this week. On the earnings front, four companies fell short of analyst expectations, while six missed revenue estimates.

Here’s a look at how the companies performed:

Among the major reporters, Freeport-McMoRan (FCX), which carries a 5.6% weighting in the index, topped Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue.

Freeport-McMoRan reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.88, beating consensus by $0.05. Revenue increased 8.3% year-over-year to $7.55 billion, exceeding estimates by $150 million. The performance was supported by higher realized prices of $6.54 per pound for copper and $4,273 per ounce for gold.

LyondellBasell (LYB) reported mixed results, with both earnings and revenue falling short of expectations. Adjusted EPS of $2.54 missed consensus by $0.01, while revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $8.50 billion but came in $390 million below estimates. The chemical producer faced weaker demand and lower polymer prices but generated $1.7 billion in operating cash flow and completed a planned €500 million debt repayment.

Nucor (NUE) delivered its strongest quarterly performance in more than three years, supported by robust domestic demand and higher realized steel prices. The steelmaker reported Q3 revenue of $11.25 billion, up 32% year-over-year and $460 million above consensus. However, adjusted EPS of $5.80 missed analyst expectations by $0.03. Steel mill shipments exceeded 7.2 million tons, while free cash flow reached $1.6 billion. Management expects fourth-quarter earnings to remain stable or increase modestly from Q3 levels. Nucor shares gained approximately 5% following the results.

Linde (LIN) reported record third-quarter results, with sales rising 9.3% year-over-year to $9.4 billion and adjusted diluted EPS increasing 9% to $4.59. Both figures exceeded Wall Street expectations, with earnings beating by $0.07 and revenue by $240 million. Growth was supported by a 5% increase in underlying sales, including a 15% rise in the electronics end market. Backed by an $11 billion project backlog, Linde raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to 8%-9%.

Sherwin-Williams (SHW) delivered mixed Q3 results, with consolidated net sales rising 7.9% year-over-year to $6.86 billion, ahead of analyst estimates. Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.63, however, missed consensus of $3.69, reflecting pressure from higher raw material costs, supply chain expenses and acquisition-related dilution. The company narrowed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $11.85-$12.15 and expects uneven demand conditions to persist into 2027.

Materials Earnings Calendar: Eight Companies Reporting Next Week

Eight S&P 500 Materials-sector companies are scheduled to report earnings next week, spanning three industries.

The Chemicals industry accounts for the largest share, with five companies on the calendar: Albemarle (ALB), Mosaic (MOS), Air Products and Chemicals (APD), CF Industries Holdings (CF) and International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF). The Containers & Packaging industry has two scheduled reporters: Amcor (AMCR) and Ball Corp. (BALL). Meanwhile, Martin Marietta Materials (MLM) is the sole company from the Construction Materials industry scheduled to report next week.

data.title: Intel wins multiple upgrades on SA after earnings-led selloff
data.description:
Intel (INTC) fell more than 28% on Friday after its Q3 2026 results, as the semiconductor giant issued an underwhelming outlook for the current quarter, prompting multiple analysts to upgrade the stock on Seeking Alpha.

The selloff, Intel’s (INTC) biggest since the 1970s, is a key buying opportunity, argued SA analyst Mike Zaccardi based on a technical analysis. “INTC remains higher by 87% for 2026, and the current plunge appears as a key technical buying opportunity in my eyes,” wrote Zaccardi as he upgraded the stock to Buy from Sell.

Analyst Bohdan Kucheriavyi upgraded Intel (INTC), noting that the company’s earnings report “was quite decent” given its topline growth of ~21% and the earnings beat of $0.12 per share on an adjusted basis. “The issue, though, is that Q4 is expected to be a much weaker quarter in comparison to Q3," the analyst wrote as they upgraded the stock to Hold from Sell.

Analyst Kenio Fontes’ upgrade was based on the stock's improved margin of safety following the selloff. “Now I’m comfortable enough to upgrade Intel to a Hold. Yet, I’m not seeing enough margin of safety to be bullish about the stock,” Fontes added as he upgraded INTC to Hold from Sell.

The Asian Investor also issued a similar upgrade, arguing that Intel’s (INTC) valuation “has normalized” after the selloff, as the stock currently trades 50% lower than its year-ago level. “With Intel’s shares down ~50% from their 1-year high at ~$142, the valuation has returned closer to the chipmaker's historical average,” the analyst wrote.

However, Seeking Alpha Investing Group Leader Quad 7 Capital downgraded INTC to Sell from Hold, noting that the stock continues to trade at a level where “perfection is fully priced in, yet the forward picture is starting to show that high expectations are not being met.” “With full-year CapEx remaining heavy and Q4 earnings power decelerating rapidly, the stock's elevated premium looks increasingly unsustainable,” Quad 7 Capital argued.

data.title: Earnings Scorecard: 11 of 17 real estate companies beat revenue estimates this week
data.description:
With the earnings season picking pace, 17 companies in the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) reported quarterly results this week, with a majority beating revenue and EPS estimates.

Of the 17 firms, revenues earned by 11 firms topped market estimates, while six companies reported lower-than-expected revenue. On the EPS front, 12 companies beat wall street estimates and three firms missed, while two companies were in line with the analyst consensus.

The XLRE has gained over 6% year-to-date, compared to the S&P 500’s more than 10% return.

Below are the key quarterly reports from the top three REIT companies this week:

American Tower (AMT): The company beat market expectation in Q3, reflecting solid leasing demand for its telecommunications infrastructure and an outperforming data centers segment. The REIT posted Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $2.87, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $2.80.  Total operating revenue came in at $2.79B, topping the $2.76B consensus. The REIT raised its full-year guidance, expecting an adjusted FFO per share of $11.04-$11.16, and adjusted EBITDA is expected to be $7.248B-$7.303B.

Vici Properties (VICI): The REIT that invests in casino and entertainment properties posted Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $0.62, in line with the Visible Alpha consensus. Total revenue was $1.07B, beating the $1.06B consensus. Raising the outlook, the company now expects 2026 adjusted FFO per share of $2.47-$2.48 vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of $2.47 and its prior outlook of $2.45-$2.47.

Federal Realty Invs Trust (FRT):  The retail REIT exceeded analyst expectations in Q3 and raised the full-year core FFO guidance to $7.54 to $7.58 from $7.48 to $7.56, above the consensus of $7.55 at the midpoint. In Q3, core FFO per diluted share reached $1.87 from $1.77 in the same period a year ago, above the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.85. Total revenue increased to $339.02M from $322.25M.

For the coming week, 10 REIT stocks are set to report their financial results, of which Realty Income (O), Vivmark Residential (VMRK), Simon Property Group (SPG), and Iron Mountain (IRM) are widely watched.
